claimed_purpose.text: Memory is provided via pluggable provider plugins, each declaring a config schema; a generic UI renderer and a REST API pair drive configuration.
Hermes Agent is described as always-on, on-device, tool-running infrastructure — the persistent runtime layer for local agentic workflows.
Memory feature page is described as covering how Hermes remembers across sessions using specific named files.
Architecture spans durable facts, procedural skills, and session search for past conversation recall
Hermes Agent includes a conversation loop, context compression, and memory as core components
Bot Mode gives each bot its own memory alongside other per-bot configuration.
Hermes is described as having a learning loop combining skills and memory.

mechanisms.text: Full session archive: every session is stored in a local SQLite database (~/.hermes/hermes_state.db) including user messages, agent responses, tool calls, reasoning steps, and token/cost data. Default retention is 90 days with automatic 24-hour pruning.

Pre-compression checkpoint: before context compression, providers are notified via on_pre_compress() with the raw transcript; a checkpoint provider must succeed when require_checkpoint=True, otherwise the uncompressed transcript is preserved.

Session messages are persisted in a SQLite `messages` table; each row carries role, content, tool_name, tool_calls, timestamp, active, compacted, and display_kind columns. This is a full message log, not a curated memory store.

The agent loaded accumulated guidance (from prior sessions) to prepare assignments for subagents without requiring the user to re-brief each worker, demonstrating retrieval of stored memory into active task context.

Live cwd state ($currentCwd) is a reactive store value that is seeded from the remembered folder; it gates to non-empty values only, meaning an absent remembered value leaves the previous gateway's folder in place.

Hermes automatically extracts reusable lessons from sessions and saves them as persistent skills — readable Markdown documents with reference files and scripts — that the agent can load for later tasks.
When a write would exceed the character limit, the tool returns an error with current entries and instructs the agent to consolidate or remove entries before retrying in the same turn.
Retrieve (prefetch): at turn start, each provider's prefetch() is called with the user query; results are merged and wrapped in a fenced <memory-context> block injected into the turn.
The agent uses distinct files for different context roles: SOUL.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md, and AGENTS.md, with documented differences in who writes each and when the agent sees them.
Within-session context is available from the conversation even before the next-session snapshot refresh; saved entries appear in the system prompt from the next session onward.
Memory is bounded: MEMORY.md capped at 2,200 characters and USER.md at 1,375; over-capacity writes fail visibly so the agent can consolidate instead of silently evicting a fact
Write path for built-in memory tools mirrors add, replace, and remove actions to the provider, with provenance metadata including write_origin, session_id, and tool_name.
Memory entries are scanned for prompt injection and credential exfiltration patterns before being accepted; matching content and invisible Unicode characters are blocked.
v0.21.0 introduced a minimum context length gate (MINIMUM_CONTEXT_LENGTH = 64_000) enforced at agent spawn time, gating which models may be used for agent-type cron jobs.
Memory is persisted to disk immediately when saved mid-session, but the system prompt snapshot is frozen at session start and does not refresh until the next session.
Compaction handoff rows (context summary content injected as role='user') are excluded from the recent-user-messages list, distinguishing them from real user turns.
Background-review harness messages (curator prompts written into real sessions by older builds) are stripped on resume to prevent replay hijacking the session
Memory has two isolated targets: 'memory' (environment facts, conventions, lessons learned) and 'user' (user identity, preferences, communication style).
Migration imports curated memory files (MEMORY.md, USER.md) and persona file (SOUL.md) — indicating memory is stored as named files, not raw transcript
Gateway switch wipes session lists and machine context but does not reset the live workspace cwd, which is the root of the stale-state continuity bug.
Context files including a global SOUL.md and project-level files are automatically injected into every conversation, functioning as a scaffold layer.
Project context files (AGENTS.md, .hermes.md) are loaded at session start with a priority chain; only one project context type is loaded per session.
Agent turns are scoped to a session identifier (HERMES_UI_SESSION_ID), which is used to route blocking UI prompts between the agent and the renderer.
A troubleshooting guide addresses memory failure modes including the agent forgetting things mid-session and a 'frozen memory snapshot' condition.
Cron jobs store a model pin (provider and model fields) in a jobs.json file that is intended to be propagated to the spawned agent subprocess.
Resume is guarded by a configurable message-count ceiling; sessions too large to reload safely raise an error rather than silently truncating
Community-reported continuity failures: recall or compaction failures, auxiliary timeout failures, memory broken after Hindsight installation
Two small markdown files (MEMORY.md and USER.md) are injected wholesale into every prompt — no retrieval step, always visible to the model.
Provider config schemas are cached by resolved file path rather than by name, so that user (per-profile) plugins are isolated per profile.
The agent wrote a CLI workaround into its long-term memory after a tool failure, and that memory outlived the fix it was responding to
Hermes Agent uses a 'local_embedded' memory provider backed by Hindsight, checked via is_available() -> _check_local_runtime()
Durable facts persisted to MEMORY.md; stable user preferences persisted to USER.md; both stored under ~/.hermes/memories/
No silent deletion: over-capacity add and replace operations return an error, requiring explicit consolidation or removal
Hub cache TTL is 5 seconds, causing the full per-plugin catalog fetch sequence to repeat on essentially every page visit
Context pollution is a named continuity failure: project-specific facts (paths, ports) appear in wrong-project sessions
Session identity is tracked with a timestamp-based session ID, indicating sessions are discrete and identified.
Memory store includes MEMORY.md and USER.md files; migratable from OpenClaw, indicating file-based persistence
Config schema is scoped per field to either 'host' (per-profile) or 'root'; flat-json storage ignores scope.
Memory entries are arbitrary text; no structured schema; tags are text prefixes in entry content
Hermes Agent supports agentic workflows including tool calls, file edits, and multi-turn plans.
Hermes Agent uses a profile-based provider configuration to point at a local model endpoint.
External memory provider plugins are supported, naming specific third-party backends.
Session persistence and resume are supported, with per-platform session tracking.
Exact duplicate entries are automatically rejected rather than silently added.
FTS5 full-text session search with LLM summarization for cross-session recall
Memory isolation is per-bot in Bot Mode; each bot has its own memory.
Hermes Agent has built-in recall that third-party tools extend.
Agent-curated memory with periodic nudges to persist knowledge
Memory provider can be disabled entirely with a CLI command.

ledger.claim: Session search uses FTS5 (SQLite full-text search) with LLM summarization, implying sessions are logged and indexed separately from curated memory
ledger.quote: FTS5 session search with LLM summarization for cross-session recall.
ledger.locator: README.md, feature list — 'A closed learning loop'
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory is stored as distinct named files (MEMORY.md, USER.md), separate from session transcripts and the persona file (SOUL.md)
ledger.quote: SOUL.md — persona file | Memories — MEMORY.md and USER.md entries
ledger.locator: README.md, Migrating from OpenClaw — 'What gets imported'
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory is retrieved per-turn via prefetch() called with the user query, merged across providers, and injected as a fenced context block before model invocation.
ledger.quote: Merge non-empty prefetch context from all providers (failures are non-fatal).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Writes (add/replace/remove) are dispatched asynchronously on a single serialized background worker to preserve turn order.
ledger.quote: The single worker also serializes writes (turn N before N+1).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Before context compression, providers are checkpointed with the transcript; the compression is aborted if a required checkpoint provider fails.
ledger.quote: With ``require_checkpoint`` at least one checkpoint provider must succeed — its exception propagates so the caller keeps the uncompressed transcript.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Session boundary triggers extraction of the old session followed by provider rebinding, run as one serialized task to prevent transcript misattribution.
ledger.quote: an ad-hoc thread raced the inline switch and misattributed transcripts.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory provider tools and system-prompt blocks are withheld together when the memory toolset is gated off, so the model is never told about tools it cannot use.
ledger.quote: provider tools and system-prompt block are both withheld.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The memory store distinguishes between a staged (pending approval) write and a committed write; only committed writes are mirrored to external providers.
ledger.quote: True only when the built-in memory tool actually committed a write. Fails closed (non-JSON, non-dict, missing ``success``, staged for approval) so providers never mirror a write that did not land.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Providers resolve storage relative to a per-profile hermes_home path, implying per-user (profile-scoped) isolation at the storage layer.
ledger.quote: injecting ``hermes_home`` so they resolve profile-scoped paths.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory retrieval is skipped for trivial prompts (greetings, acknowledgements, empty input, slash commands) to avoid stale context on one-word replies.
ledger.quote: skipping recall saves a round-trip and keeps stale context from derailing one-word replies
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Prefetch is designed to run in the background and return cached results rather than blocking the turn.
ledger.quote: Must be fast — recall in the background and return cached results
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The write path supports three operations: add, replace, and remove, mirrored to providers with provenance metadata.
ledger.quote: Mirror a built-in memory-tool write (``action``: add | replace | remove; ``target``: memory | user; ``metadata``: provenance such as write_origin, session_id, tool_name).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Isolation is enforced at the profile level via ContextVar-scoped HERMES_HOME; failing to propagate context causes silent fallback to default profile.
ledger.quote: a worker started with an empty context silently lands on the default profile (or fails closed on secrets)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: All memory-provider background threads (prefetch, sync, writer loops) must use spawn_context_thread to inherit the caller's contextvars.
ledger.quote: Every memory-provider background job (prefetch, sync, writer loops) must go through this.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Session switch is handled without process teardown, distinguishing new-conversation reset (flush buffers) from transcript rewind (same session id, truncated history).
ledger.quote: ``reset`` is True only for a genuinely new conversation (flush buffers); ``rewound``: same id but the transcript was truncated.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Pre-compression v2 checkpoint adds fail-closed behavior and normalized evidence handoff; v1 is best-effort.
ledger.quote: v1 = best-effort on_pre_compress() with the raw message list; v2 = opt-in fail-closed checkpoint (normalized evidence handoff + strict-mode failure propagation).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory configuration uses a plugin architecture with per-provider declarative schemas and a REST API for UI-driven config management.
ledger.quote: Declarative config schema for memory provider plugins: each declares its fields in a `config_schema.py` beside `__init__.py`; one generic renderer and one `GET/PUT /api/memory/providers/{name}/config` pair drive the UI.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Isolation fields available at initialization include per-user (user_id, user_id_alt), per-session (session_id, parent_session_id), per-agent (agent_identity, agent_context, agent_workspace) dimensions.
ledger.quote: may include ``agent_context`` ("primary" | "subagent" | "cron" | "flush" — skip writes for non-primary contexts), ``agent_identity``, ``agent_workspace``, ``parent_session_id``, ``user_id``, ``user_id_alt``.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Resume reloads the transcript up to a configurable ceiling; exceeding it raises an error with an explicit user action
ledger.quote: This session is too long to reload safely ({message_count} messages; limit {limit}). Start a fresh chat and use `hermes sessions export` to keep a copy, or raise the limit with `hermes config set sessions.max_resume_messages 0`.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Compression archives rows and stores a _compressed_summary inline; archived rows are distinguished by the 'active' column
ledger.quote: ``active`` rides along so a display read can split compaction-archived rows without a second query.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: A background curator review harness existed that wrote curator turns into real sessions; those turns are stripped on load to prevent replay
ledger.quote: Persisted harness prompt (older builds wrote the forked curator's turns into real sessions; replaying them hijacks the session).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The curator harness prompted the model to update a skill library and consider saving to memory, indicating a separate curated-memory write path exists outside this file
ledger.quote:
_REVIEW_HARNESS_PREFIXES = (
    "Review the conversation above and update the skill library",
    "Review the conversation above and consider saving to memory",
)

ledger.claim: System prompts are deduplicated by SHA-256 hash; orphaned prompts are deleted when no session references them
ledger.quote: DELETE FROM system_prompts WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE sessions.system_prompt_hash = system_prompts.hash)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Title authority levels prevent user-typed titles from being overwritten by LLM-derived auto-titles
ledger.quote: auto-titling may only replace a strictly lower-authority title (``derived`` -> ``llm`` once; never a user-typed name).
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Hermes Agent persists the full message log (role, content, tool_name, tool_calls, timestamp, active/compacted flags) in a SQLite messages table per session — this is a log, not curated memory.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Model-facing scaffold messages (display_kind='hidden') are excluded from search, preventing internal system messages from surfacing as memory hits.
ledger.quote:
# display_kind="hidden" rows are model-facing scaffolding the person never saw; a hit would confuse.
            where.append("COALESCE(m.display_kind, '') <> 'hidden'")
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Compaction produces summary handoff rows injected as role='user'; these are identified and excluded from the recent-user-message list so undo/rewind counts stay correct.
ledger.quote:
if ContextCompressor._is_context_summary_content(decoded):
                continue  # compaction handoff — never a user-originated turn

ledger.claim: Search retrieve policy is on-demand (called explicitly); no evidence on this page of automatic injection into every turn.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Tool-result rows are indexed with a truncated prefix only; full tool content is accessible only via explicit tool-role LIKE scan, not standard FTS retrieval.
ledger.quote: New oversized tool results index only a bounded prefix; an explicit tool-role search is the opt-in full-body path and scans canonical rows via LIKE.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Session is the isolation unit: all message storage and retrieval is scoped to session_id; cross-session search is possible but filtered by source, role, and time bounds.
ledger.quote:
source_filter: List[str] = None, exclude_sources: List[str] = None,

ledger.claim: Project-local memory providers require explicit opt-in via HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS to prevent implicit activation.
ledger.quote: if not _env_enabled("HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS"): return None

ledger.claim: Skills registered by an inactive provider are pruned from the registry; isolation is per Hermes home.
ledger.quote: pruning under one multiplexed profile must only retract that profile's provider skills, never a sibling profile's.

ledger.claim: Provider availability is probed without importing, to avoid running arbitrary code at discovery time.
ledger.quote: resolved WITHOUT importing it (discovery runs from the dashboard/argparse before a provider is selected; importing every candidate would run arbitrary code)

ledger.quote: Cached by resolved file path, not name: user plugins are per-profile.

ledger.claim: Write path supports add, replace (substring match), and remove (substring match); no read action exists.
ledger.quote:
add — Add a new memory entry
replace — Replace an existing entry with updated content (uses substring matching via old_text)
remove — Remove an entry that's no longer relevant (uses substring matching via old_text)

There is no read action — memory content is automatically injected into the system prompt at session start.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Frozen snapshot: memory is loaded once at session start and does not update in the system prompt mid-session; disk writes are immediate but only visible next session.
ledger.quote: The system prompt injection is captured once at session start and never changes mid-session. This is intentional — it preserves the LLM's prefix cache for performance. When the agent adds/removes memory entries during a session, the changes are persisted to disk immediately but won't appear in the system prompt until the next session starts.
ledger.locator: How Memory Appears in the System Prompt — Frozen snapshot pattern
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget path: remove action deletes entries from the store; journey delete removes memory chunks permanently (skills are archived/restorable).
ledger.quote: remove — Remove an entry that's no longer relevant... hermes journey delete <node> [-y] Delete a node. Skills are archived (restorable), memory chunks are removed.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conflict / capacity management: writes that exceed the character limit are rejected with an error and current entries list; the agent must consolidate or remove entries before retrying in the same turn.
ledger.quote: when a write would exceed the limit, the memory tool returns an error instead of silently dropping entries. The agent then makes room itself — consolidating or removing entries in the same turn before retrying
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Duplicate prevention: exact duplicate entries are rejected automatically.
ledger.quote: The memory system automatically rejects exact duplicate entries. If you try to add content that already exists, it returns success with a 'no duplicate added' message.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Isolation is per profile (Hermes home directory); two agents sharing a home will corrupt each other's memory state.
ledger.quote: Memory is scoped per profile by design — give a second agent its own profile, and if they need shared memory, use an external memory provider instead.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Session search (separate from memory) uses SQLite FTS5 over all past sessions, returning raw messages with no LLM summarization; it is on-demand, not always injected.
ledger.quote:
All CLI and messaging sessions are stored in SQLite (~/.hermes/state.db) with FTS5 full-text search
Search queries return actual messages from the DB — no LLM summarization, no truncation
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Background review runs after each turn and may write memory entries or skills; it operates as a consent-aware learning loop and can be gated by write_approval.
ledger.quote: This is Hermes' consent-aware learning loop: repeated corrections and durable workflow lessons become compact memory entries or procedural skills, while write_approval can stage those writes for review before they affect future sessions.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Write approval gate: write_approval: true stages all writes (foreground and background review) for explicit user approval; /memory pending lists them tagged [auto] for background writes.
ledger.quote: If you'd rather approve saves first, set memory.write_approval: true. It's a simple on/off gate applied to both foreground turns and the background review... /memory pending # list staged memory writes (auto ones tagged [auto])
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory stores are separated by semantic type: 'memory' target for environment/workflow facts, 'user' target for user identity and preferences.
ledger.quote:
memory — Agent's Personal Notes
For information the agent needs to remember about the environment, workflows, and lessons learned...
user — User Profile
For information about the user's identity, preferences, and communication style
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieve policy: memory is always injected (fixed cost ~1,300 tokens per session); session_search is adaptive/on-demand and free of token cost until invoked.
ledger.quote: Memory is for critical facts that should always be in context... Token cost Fixed per session (~1,300 tokens) On-demand (searched when needed)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Security scanning blocks prompt injection, credential exfiltration patterns, SSH backdoors, and invisible Unicode in memory entries before persistence.
ledger.quote: Memory entries are scanned for injection and exfiltration patterns before being accepted, since they're injected into the system prompt. Content matching threat patterns (prompt injection, credential exfiltration, SSH backdoors) or containing invisible Unicode characters is blocked.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The agent proactively saves without being asked, including user preferences, environment facts, corrections, conventions, completed work, and explicit requests.

The agent saves automatically — you don't need to ask. It saves when it learns:
User preferences... Environment facts... Corrections... Conventions... Completed work... Explicit requests

ledger.quote: USER.md — User profile — your name, role, preferences, communication style, expectations — The agent, via the memory tool … MEMORY.md — Agent's personal notes — environment facts, project conventions, tool quirks, things learned — The agent, via the memory tool
